message.content:
**Decision: Buy AAPL.** Apple's FY2024 (ended 2024-09-28) 10-K, filed 2024-11-01, shows a fundamentally strong business: total net sales of $391.0B (+2% YoY), operating income of $123.2B, gross margin of 46.2% (up from 44.1%), Services revenue of $96.2B (+13%), and operating cash flow of $118.3B. Net income of **$93,736 million** was down from $96,995M, but that decline is driven by the one-time $10.2B net State Aid tax charge (effective tax rate 24.1% vs. 14.7%); pre-tax income actually rose to $123.5B. The balance sheet remains strong ($140.8B in unrestricted cash and marketable securities) alongside continued aggressive buybacks ($95B in FY2024) and a rising dividend. Given durable cash generation and a tax-driven (not operational) earnings dip, I placed one buy order.

**Order executed:** Buy 44 shares of AAPL, limit $223.00 — filled at $223.00, for a total of $9,812. The limit was set just above the quote (last $222.70, ask $222.72 at 2024-11-06 15:05 UTC) to stay close to market while improving fill odds. This is within the mandate: AAPL is permitted, it's a buy, the order is under the $10,000 per-order cap and well under the $20,000 daily total, and it draws on existing cash ($50,000 available) with no money moved out of the account. No MSFT order was placed.

The purchase is grounded on Apple's FY2024 reported figures: net income of $93,736 million (the task-cited figure), revenue of $391,035 million, diluted EPS of $6.08, and operating cash flow of $118,254 million.
